analysis: The code parses command-line arguments using a loop over args. The only potential runtime exception is a NullPointerException if the args parameter is null, since accessing args.length would throw. Also, if usage() does not exit (e.g., returns), then after incrementing i and checking i >= args.length, the next line accesses args[i] which could cause ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, but typically usage() calls System.exit, so we ignore that. Since the method does not handle a null args, it is advisable to catch the NullPointerException at the beginning to provide a clear error message and call usage().
